plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only deliverable; no execution performed, no results reported)

Research question: Does SPAG's adversarial setup (Adversarial Taboo: GPT-4 imitation learning followed by self-play on game episodes) yield superior reasoning improvements versus non-adversarial setups (20-Question, Guess-My-City)?

Primary contrast (fixed by task context): SPAG/adversarial vs. each non-adversarial arm. The no-game / imitation-only arms are SECONDARY comparisons guarding against a "more game data of any kind" confound.

──────────────────────────────────────────
A. ASSUMED DESIGN PARAMETERS (not source-verified; each flagged [A#], each with a justified default and sensitivity note)
──────────────────────────────────────────
[A1] Base model: Llama-3-8B-Instruct. Default because SPAG-class work targets open ~7–8B instruct models with GPT-4 as teacher. Sensitivity: repeat the best-contrast arm pair on a second family (e.g., Mistral-7B-Instruct or Qwen2-7B-Instruct) at reduced episode budget; conclusions should be treated as preliminary if only one model family is affordable.
[A2] GPT-4 role: teacher/opponent generating stage-1 episodes for BOTH game roles (via persona prompts), plus a judging function in stage 2 (rule-based verifier for hard constraints — e.g., "did the defender utter the target word" — with GPT-4 as arbiter for ambiguous cases only, to cut cost). Sensitivity: a fully rule-based judge variant; if conclusions flip, judge noise is a threat.
[A3] Imitation covers both roles per arm (attacker+defender for Taboo; questioner+answerer for 20-Question and Guess-My-City). Sensitivity: single-role imitation would halve stage-1 data; note as a limitation if budget forces it.
[A4] Stage transition criterion: FIXED episode budget (not a win-rate threshold) — stage 1: 8,000 GPT-4-played episodes per arm; stage 2: 4 self-play rounds × 10,000 episodes with distillation after each round. Fixed budgets guarantee cross-arm comparability. Sensitivity: under a smaller budget (see F), scale to 2,000 + 4×2,500; all arms scale identically, so contrasts remain internally valid; absolute gains will shrink.
[A5] Word/topic lists: Taboo target-word list and city list are public/common-noun and world-city lists (e.g., ~500 items each) matched on corpus frequency and familiarity; 20-Question uses the same noun list as Taboo's target words as question topics. 80/20 train/held-out split of lists.
[A6] SFT hyperparameters: full fine-tune, 3 epochs, lr 2e-5 cosine, batch 128 episodes-equivalent, identical across arms; self-play distillation uses rejection-filtered transcripts (judge-verified legal episodes only).
[A7] Compute assumption for feasibility: 8×A100-80GB (or equivalent ~640 GPU-hr budget) plus limited GPT-4 API budget (~$500 default, ~$150 reduced variant).
[A8] Evaluation decoding: greedy (temperature 0), fixed 3-shot prompts, identical across arms.

──────────────────────────────────────────
B. CONDITION MATRIX (all arms share [A1], [A6], [A8] and matched budgets)
──────────────────────────────────────────
Data/compute matching rule: identical number of training episodes, identical total fine-tuning tokens, identical GPT-4-transcript share, identical optimizer steps. Because episode lengths differ across games, the binding constraint is TOTAL TOKENS: each arm is padded/truncated (by repeating or sampling episodes) to the same token budget T ≈ 29M tokens (≈5M imitation + ≈24M self-play per [A4]).

| Arm | Game | Stage 1 (GPT-4 imitation) | Stage 2 (self-play) | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (PRIMARY) | Adversarial Taboo (SPAG-style) | 8k episodes, both roles | 4 rounds × 10k episodes + distill | adversarial |
| 2 (PRIMARY) | 20-Question | 8k episodes, both roles | 4 rounds × 10k episodes + distill | non-adversarial |
| 3 (PRIMARY) | Guess-My-City | 8k episodes, both roles | 4 rounds × 10k episodes + distill | non-adversarial |
| 4 (secondary) | Taboo, imitation-only | 8k episodes | none (train on stage-1 only, token-matched by padding with stage-1 data) | control |
| 5 (secondary) | Taboo self-play vs. fixed/random opponent (frozen stage-1 snapshot as opponent; opponent rotates among snapshots to avoid trivial exploitation) | 8k episodes | 4 rounds × 10k vs. fixed opponent | control |
| 6 (secondary, optional) | No-game SFT on generic instruction data token-matched to T | — | — | control |

Interaction-step matching: all self-play arms (1,2,3,5) run the same number of game turns per episode (Taboo capped at 12 turns; 20-Question at 20 yes/no turns but token-normalized so total interactive tokens match; Guess-My-City capped at 12 turns). Judge calls counted uniformly.

──────────────────────────────────────────
C. PER-ARM PIPELINE SPECIFICATION
──────────────────────────────────────────
Stage 0 (setup): build word/city/topic lists [A5]; split 80/20; pre-register prompts (system prompts define roles and rules identically templated across games).
Stage 1 (imitation, all arms 1–5): generate GPT-4-played episodes [A2][A3]; filter illegal/degenerate episodes (rule verifier); SFT on transcripts (loss on assistant-role tokens only).
Stage 2 (self-play, arms 1,2,3,5): each round — (i) sample held-out and train-list items; (ii) student copy A vs. student copy B play N episodes (arm 5: vs. frozen snapshot); (iii) judge scores episodes [A2]; (iv) distill judge-passing transcripts back into the single student via SFT (same lr/epochs [A6]); (v) log win rates and language-quality stats (repetition, degeneration) for stability monitoring [E3].
Stage 3 (freeze final checkpoint; identical eval pipeline for all arms).

──────────────────────────────────────────
D. EVALUATION PLAN
──────────────────────────────────────────
D1. Primary reasoning benchmarks (primary endpoint): GSM8K full test and MATH-500 — metric: exact-match accuracy, greedy decoding [A8]. Rationale: multi-step reasoning where SPAG-class claims concentrate.
D2. In-domain transfer / generalization: (i) held-out 20% of game lists — in-game win rate vs. a frozen GPT-4 opponent (manipulation check: confirms the adversarial arm actually learned the adversarial skill); (ii) unseen-topic game variants to test that gains are not list-memorization.
D3. Out-of-domain transfer (secondary): Big-Bench-Hard 3-task subset and ARC-Challenge, same decoding.
D4. Contamination check (pre-training, blocking): n-gram (8-gram) and embedding-similarity screen of every game target word/city and every system prompt against GSM8K/MATH/BBH/ARC items; any game item whose surface form appears in a benchmark item is removed from training lists and logged. Report contamination rates per arm.
D5. Style-control probe (secondary): a "GPT-4-style matching" diagnostic — measure response-style divergence (length, hedging, formatting) of each arm vs. its stage-1 teacher data, to detect whether gains track style imitation rather than reasoning [E1].

──────────────────────────────────────────
E. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN
──────────────────────────────────────────
E1. Primary endpoint: Δaccuracy = post-training accuracy − same-checkpoint pre-training accuracy on D1 (pooled GSM8K+MATH-500, and reported per-benchmark). Primary hypotheses: H1: Arm1 > Arm2; H2: Arm1 > Arm3 (two co-primary comparisons).
E2. Seeds: 3 independent training seeds minimum (5 preferred for arms 1–3 only, given budget); pre/post evaluated per seed.
E3. Tests: per seed, question-level paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples) for Δaccuracy CIs; across seeds, mixed-effects logistic regression (correct ~ arm + (1|question) + (1|seed) + benchmark fixed effect) with planned contrasts; report Hedges' g effect sizes with seed-level CIs. Multiplicity: Holm correction across the two co-primary comparisons at α=0.05; all other comparisons (arm1 vs. 4/5/6; D3; D2-i) labeled exploratory. Decision rule: adversarial superiority claimed only if both H1 and H2 survive Holm correction in the predicted direction; if only one survives, report as partial evidence with explicit caveat.
E4. Secondary analyses: mediation-style check — does arm 1's in-game win-rate gain (D2-i) correlate with reasoning Δ across seeds (tests the hypothesized mechanism); arm 4 vs. arm 1 isolates the self-play contribution; arm 5 vs. arm 1 isolates the adversarial-opponent contribution; arm 6 bounds generic-data effects.

──────────────────────────────────────────
F. CONTROLS AND VALIDITY
──────────────────────────────────────────
E1 — Teacher-style leakage: all stage-1 data come from the same GPT-4 teacher with matched token budgets in every arm [B], so imitation-style content is equated; the D5 style probe detects residual style-driven gains; arm 6 (generic GPT-4-distilled SFT) bounds pure style distillation.
E2 — Topic-distribution differences across games: Taboo words and 20-Question topics are drawn from the SAME noun list [A5]; city list matched on frequency/familiarity; the same 80/20 split indices are reused across arms; token-budget matching removes length confounds.
E3 — Self-play instability: fixed episode budgets (not adaptive stopping) [A4]; rejection filtering of degenerate transcripts; KL-to-SFT-init anchor in distillation (implicit via SFT-only updates on filtered data); monitor per-round win rate, response length, and repetition rate; pre-registered early-stop rule only if degeneration is detected (applied symmetrically to all self-play arms).
E4 — Data-quantity confound: token-matched [B]; arm 4 shows imitation-only ceiling at the same tokens.
E5 — Judge bias across game types: rule-based hard-constraint checks where possible [A2]; judge prompts identical in structure; a 200-episode human-audit of judge agreement reported per arm.
E6 — Decoding/prompting confounds: identical eval prompts, few-shot exemplars, decoding [A8]; eval harness blind to arm identity.

──────────────────────────────────────────
G. FEASIBILITY (bounds under [A7]; NOT executed here — this workspace has no GPU, no ML stack, and no repository content)
──────────────────────────────────────────
Rollout volumes per arm: stage 1 ≈ 8k episodes × ~600 tokens ≈ 5M tokens; stage 2 ≈ 40k episodes × ~600 tokens ≈ 24M tokens; total ≈ 29M generated tokens per arm; ×5 arms ×3 seeds ≈ ~435M inference tokens. At ~1,500–2,500 tok/s aggregate on 8×A100 with vLLM-class serving, self-play generation is ≈ 50–80 GPU-hours total; SFT (≈29M tokens × 3 epochs per arm, 8B model full FT) ≈ 10–15 GPU-hours per arm → overall ≈ 200–400 GPU-hours, within the [A7] 640 GPU-hour budget. GPT-4 API: only stage 1 (≈5M tokens × 3 game arms + judge arbiter calls) ≈ 16–20M tokens ≈ $300–600 at GPT-4-class pricing; reduced-budget variant (2k episodes) ≈ $150.
Sensitivity note (per researcher instruction): under a 4× smaller budget, scale [A4] to 2k + 4×2.5k episodes; all contrasts remain internally valid because matching is preserved, but absolute effect sizes shrink and seed-level CIs widen — the design then detects only large (>2–3 point) accuracy differences; report as underpowered rather than null.
Environment constraint: this workspace (no GPU, no torch, network disabled, only task.json present) cannot execute any part of this design; the deliverable is a specification executable in principle by a team with the [A7] resources. No experiment was run and no results are claimed.

Assumption register recap: [A1]–[A8] are assumed defaults with sensitivity notes; the only fixed (task-context) requirement is the primary adversarial-vs-non-adversarial contrast. No SPAG mechanics in this document should be cited as source-verified.
